messages:
marta: Quick heads-up @here — tomorrow morning (08:00 PT) we're rolling out the new org-scoped GitHub App + central webhook relay for CI delivery. This replaces per-repo webhooks and repo-level deploy keys. :loud_sound:

samir: Nice. What's the main driver? Security/maintenance?

marta: Both. Fewer secrets to manage, better observability, and we can push schema-safe retries. Also lets us rotate CI signing keys without touching each repo.

linda: Are repo admins going to need to do anything?

marta: Yes, two small steps: install the GitHub App for your repo/org (link in docs), and ensure the org allows third-party apps. We'll send a PR with the minimal permissions.

kevin: What about existing per-repo webhooks we added for integrations? Any auto-migration?

marta: We'll auto-create relay registrations for repos that opted-in during the beta. For others we will create draft webhook records and ping repo admins via GH issues. No silent removals.

sofia: CI impact — will builds be paused/restarted?

marta: Short answer: no long downtime. CI will continue to consume events via the relay. There will be a brief switch (a few seconds) when we flip routing. We'll move in batches and monitor.

jason: Who do we ping if something breaks during rollout?

marta: @kevin and @samir are on-call for the rollout. Also our rollback plan lives in the doc. If your pipeline breaks, post here and mention @devops-bot or call pager.

samir: Putting quick checklist here for repo admins:
- Install GitHub App (org/repo level)
- Verify webhook delivery URL in repo settings (should show relay.redwood.internal)
- Confirm no legacy deploy keys used by CI jobs

kevin: Sample command for self-hosted runner owners to fetch new ephemeral token: 

```bash
# run on runner host
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_AGENT_KEY" \
  https://relay.redwood.internal/v1/runner/token | jq -r .token
```

linda: Will we rotate CI agent keys during this?

marta: Yes, starting next week we'll rotate long-lived CI_AGENT_KEYs into short-lived agent tokens. Agent config will still use the same env var name but the token will expire hourly. The agent has auto-refresh.

sofia: Any perf implications?

marta: Relay adds a tiny hop but improves throughput via connection pooling. End-to-end latency should be ~+10-30ms on average, but we gain far fewer dropped events.

devops-bot: Scheduled job created: rollout/relay-switch-2026-03-25 08:00 PT — target batch size 150 repos. Contact: @kevin, @samir.

jason: Example webhook config we'll apply (for reference):

```json
{"url":"https://relay.redwood.internal/h/REPO_ID","content_type":"json","insecure_ssl":"0","events":["push","pull_request"],"active":true}
```

marta: Docs: https://intranet.redwood.com/docs/devex/relay-github-app — includes install links, permission matrix, and rollback steps. Please read before tomorrow.

kevin: Rollback plan (short):
1) Pause relay routing for affected batch
2) Re-enable per-repo webhook targets (we keep backups)
3) Re-create any missing deploy keys (audit logs will show removals)

sofia: Thanks — I'll coordinate with the product infra team to watch the critical pipelines during the flip.

marta: Thanks everyone. We'll post a short post-mortem if anything unexpected happens. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Deployment note: relay-service v2.1.0 scheduled to deploy at 07:30 PT (pre-rollout smoke checks).

samir: I'll be online at rollout time. Ping me if you see >0.5% failure rate on CI events.

marta: Awesome. If you haven't installed the app yet, please do so now — will re-run the installer for any leftover repos after the batch.
